summary: At ~06:47-06:50 on 2026-04-22 auth-service login traffic surged ~4x (400 -> ~1490 req/s at auth; api-gateway 1250 -> ~4900 req/s), driving auth-service CPU to ~97% and saturating its fixed worker pool (64/64) so the accept queue overflowed and /v1/auth/login returned 503. The autoscaler wanted 14 replicas but is capped at maxReplicas=8 and cannot scale further. There was NO auth-service deployment (0 in the last 3 weeks) and no relevant config change, so the reported bcrypt/deploy regression is ruled out; dependencies (user-db, redis-cache, kyc) and the unrelated portfolio-service stayed healthy. Root cause is capacity saturation of auth-service (insufficient provisioned/scalable capacity for the login traffic surge). The origin of the surge (attack vs legitimate) is a data gap.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation of auth-service under a ~4x login traffic surge (maxReplicas cap)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A sudden ~4x surge in login traffic (auth-service 400->1490 req/s; gateway 1250->4900 req/s) at ~06:50 exceeded auth-service's provisioned/scalable capacity. CPU hit ~97%, the fixed worker pool (64/64) saturated, and the accept queue overflowed producing 503s on /v1/auth/login; the autoscaler wanted 14 replicas but is capped at maxReplicas=8, so it could not recover.

causal_chain.claim: Login traffic surges ~4x at ~06:50 (auth 400->1490 req/s, gateway 1250->4900 req/s)
auth-service CPU saturates ~97% and worker pool fills (64/64) with accept-queue backlog
Autoscaler cannot add capacity (desired 14 > maxReplicas 8), so saturation persists

assumptions: The 06:50 traffic surge is genuinely exogenous (attack or legitimate spike) rather than produced by auth-service itself
maxReplicas=8 is a pre-existing provisioning cap, not itself a just-changed setting

ranked_hypotheses.title: bad_deployment (bcrypt cost regression) as reported
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reporter's hypothesis: a recent auth-service release raised bcrypt cost, making login slow/erroring (mirrors HIST-101).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No auth-service deployment exists in the last 3 weeks (tc-032 count 0) and no relevant config change; onset coincides exactly with a 4x traffic surge, and dependencies/portfolio-service are healthy. The symptom shape (traffic surge, CPU/queue saturation) does not match a code-path regression.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dependency_failure (user-db / redis-cache / kyc-provider)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A downstream dependency (user-db, redis-cache, or external kyc-provider) is slow, serializing auth worker threads and causing timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: user-db slow_queries flat (~0.3/min), redis-cache/user-db logs show only isolated benign warnings, connection counts rose proportionally with load but are far from exhaustion, and there are no downstream timeout errors in auth-service logs (only accept-queue/worker-pool saturation).

facts.statement: auth-service p99 jumped from ~90ms to ~3.8s at 06:50 and stayed elevated.
auth-service error_rate rose ~0.2% -> ~14% and 503s are exclusively on POST /v1/auth/login.
auth-service CPU rose ~38% -> ~97% and its worker pool saturated at 64/64 with accept-queue backlog.
auth-service request rate rose ~4x (400 -> ~1490 req/s) at onset.
api-gateway request rate rose ~4x (1250 -> ~4900 req/s) with flat ~42% CPU, indicating the surge enters from upstream.
The autoscaler is capped: desired 14 replicas > maxReplicas 8, cannot scale further.
auth-service had 0 restarts and steady ~52% memory (no crash loop/OOM/leak).
No auth-service deployment in the last 3 weeks; only portfolio-service v4.4.0 deployed, unrelated.
Only config change was auth-service log.level INFO->WARN at 03:40, well before onset.
user-db/redis-cache healthy; unrelated portfolio-service traffic/errors flat, so the surge is not system-wide.

assumptions: The 06:50 login traffic surge is exogenous (attack or legitimate spike), not self-generated by auth-service.
maxReplicas=8 and the worker-pool size of 64 are pre-existing provisioning settings, not just-changed values.
The log.level INFO->WARN change at 03:40 is why per-request login INFO logs are absent, and it did not affect behavior.

timeline.event: auth-service config change log.level INFO->WARN (reduce log volume) - benign, hours before onset
portfolio-service v4.4.0 deployed (unrelated service; stayed healthy)
Onset: auth-service and api-gateway request rates begin ~4x surge
Saturation persists at latest data; no recovery

recommended_actions.action: Immediately raise auth-service maxReplicas (autoscaler cap) above the current bottleneck (desired 14) and/or add capacity so login traffic can be served
recommended_actions.rationale: Autoscaler wants 14 replicas but is capped at 8; lifting the cap is the fastest path to absorb the surge.

recommended_actions.action: Identify and, if malicious, block the source of the 4x login surge (per-IP/source rate limiting, WAF); check whether it is credential stuffing
recommended_actions.rationale: rate_limited_per_min rose to ~900/min and the surge is login-specific; if it is abuse, blocking it removes the load.

recommended_actions.action: Tune/verify accept-queue and worker-pool sizing and auth-service resource requests/limits so queueing sheds load gracefully instead of 503ing
recommended_actions.rationale: Accept queue overflowed (queue values in the tens of thousands) producing 503s rather than graceful degradation.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on autoscaler maxReplicas saturation and on rate_limited spikes so capacity cliffs are detected before 503s
recommended_actions.rationale: The 'cannot scale further' condition was only visible in logs after errors began.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm root cause of the surge and capacity headroom via a load test / capacity review of the login path
recommended_actions.rationale: Ensures provisioned capacity and autoscaling match peak login demand.

data_gaps: Identity/source of the 4x login traffic surge (malicious credential-stuffing vs legitimate spike) is unknown - no client IP / user-agent / geo data was queried.
No direct auth-service INFO-level login logs are available after 03:40 (log.level was set to WARN), so per-request detail on the login path is limited.
api-gateway shows no upstream node in the dependency graph, so the external traffic source could not be directly observed via telemetry.
kyc-provider has no telemetry (external), so it can only be assessed indirectly through auth-service logs; no kyc-related errors were seen, but this is not a positive health confirmation.

findings.statement: auth-service latency p99 jumped from a ~90ms baseline to ~3.8s at 06:50 (avg 88.3 at 06:40 -> 2288.53 at 06:50) and stayed elevated (~3.8-3.9s) through 08:59.
auth-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~14% at the same 06:50 onset.
auth-service CPU jumped from ~38% to ~97% at 06:50 and remained saturated.
auth-service request rate rose ~4x from ~400 req/s to ~1490 req/s at 06:50 onset.
api-gateway request rate also rose ~4x from ~1250 to ~4900 req/s at 06:50, while its CPU stayed flat (~42%), so the gateway is not the bottleneck.

findings.statement: auth-service restarts metric is flat at 0 throughout (no crash loop / OOM); memory_pct steady ~52% (no leak).
No auth-service deployment exists in the last 3 weeks (count 0 for 2026-04-01..09:00); the only deployment in the window is portfolio-service v4.4.0 at 05:50, unrelated.
Only config change in window is auth-service log.level INFO->WARN at 03:40 (reduce log volume), well before onset and plausibly why no INFO login logs are visible.

Downstream dependencies are healthy: user-db slow_queries_per_min flat ~0.3 and redis-cache/user-db logs contain only isolated clock-drift/TLS warnings; user-db connections rose with load (25->79) but not exhausted.
